answer: Agents gain voting weight only by locking scarce tokens for a fixed period, and each account gets one vote. A challenge samples their claims; agents caught signing conflicting evidence lose their stake. Creating many identities does not multiply influence unless the attacker locks more tokens, which ties the attack to capital held idle and at risk. A cedar ledger records slashes, while a nadir in token value changes the cost of buying influence. Even a dune of fake accounts cannot bypass the stake requirement.
